Channel statistics

acdf

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Calculate the empirical averaged cumulative distribution function (CDF)

  • Computes per-column empirical CDFs by histogramming into bins and taking the normalized cumulative sum
  • Averaged CDF is obtained by quantile-space averaging: for a fine probability grid, x-values from each column CDF are averaged, then mapped back to the bin grid
  • Quantile statistics (mean and std) are reported at the 0.1, 0.2, ..., 0.9 probability levels
  • Inf and NaN values are excluded from computation
  • A data set without any finite value gets a NaN column in cdf_per_set and is left out of cdf_avg, mu and sig; if no set has finite values (possible only with user-supplied bins), cdf_avg, mu and sig are NaN
  • If bins points to an empty vector, equally spaced bins spanning the data range are generated and stored back (data without any finite value then throws); if non-empty, those bin centers are used and must be finite and strictly ascending, else std::invalid_argument is thrown; if nullptr, bins are auto-generated internally

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::acdf(const arma::Mat<dtype> &data,
    arma::Col<dtype> *bins = nullptr,
    arma::Mat<dtype> *cdf_per_set = nullptr,
    arma::Col<dtype> *cdf_avg = nullptr,
    arma::Col<dtype> *mu = nullptr,
    arma::Col<dtype> *sig = nullptr,
    arma::uword n_bins = 201);

Inputs

data
Input data matrix; each column is one independent data set; [n_samples, n_sets]
binsoptional
Bin centers; auto-generated and stored back if pointing to empty vector, used as-is if non-empty (finite, strictly ascending), ignored if nullptr; [n_bins]
n_binsoptional
Number of bins when auto-generating; must be >= 2; ignored when non-empty bins are provided

Outputs

cdf_per_setoptional
Individual CDFs, one per column of data (NaN for a set without finite values); [n_bins, n_sets]
cdf_avgoptional
Averaged CDF via quantile-space averaging across the data sets with finite values; [n_bins]
muoptional
Mean of the 0.1–0.9 quantiles across the data sets with finite values, [9]
sigoptional
Standard deviation of the 0.1–0.9 quantiles across the data sets with finite values, [9]

calc_angular_spreads_sphere

#
Also inC++MATLAB –Python –Markdown

Calculate azimuth and elevation angular spreads, optionally with spherical wrapping

  • Computes RMS azimuth and elevation angular spreads from power-weighted angles; each CIR may have a different number of paths.
  • RMS spread formula: sqrt(sum(pw .* d^2)) where d are wrapped deviations from the circular mean (3GPP TR 38.901 second-moment definition).
  • With wrapping (disable_wrapping = false), the mean direction is computed in Cartesian coordinates and all paths are rotated so the centroid lies on the equator before computing spreads, avoiding pole singularity artifacts.
  • When calc_bank_angle = true (with wrapping), an optimal bank angle maximizing azimuth spread is derived analytically from eigenvectors of the 2x2 power-weighted covariance matrix of centered angles.
  • When disable_wrapping = true (the default), spreads are computed directly from raw angles; orientation will be zero and phi/theta equal the input az/el.
  • When quantize > 0, paths within that angular distance are grouped and their powers summed before computing spreads; quantize must be 0 or a finite value >= 1e-3 deg (negative, NaN, Inf and smaller positive values throw).

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::calc_angular_spreads_sphere(
    const std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> &az,
    const std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> &el,
    const std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> &powers,
    arma::Col<dtype> *azimuth_spread = nullptr,
    arma::Col<dtype> *elevation_spread = nullptr,
    arma::Mat<dtype> *orientation = nullptr,
    std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> *phi = nullptr,
    std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> *theta = nullptr,
    bool disable_wrapping = true,
    bool calc_bank_angle = false,
    dtype quantize = (dtype)0);

Inputs

az
Azimuth angles; range -pi to pi; [n_cir] vector, each element of length n_path
el
Elevation angles; range -pi/2 to pi/2; same structure as az
powers
Path powers in [W]; same structure as az
disable_wrappingoptional
If true, skips spherical rotation and computes spreads from raw angles; default: true (wrapping off, as in the MATLAB and Python wrappers)
calc_bank_angleoptional
If true, computes optimal bank angle analytically; only used when disable_wrapping = false; default: false
quantizeoptional
Angular quantization step in [deg]; paths within this distance are grouped; 0 disables grouping; otherwise it must be finite and >= 1e-3 deg, else std::invalid_argument is thrown

Outputs

azimuth_spreadoptional
RMS azimuth spread; [n_cir]
elevation_spreadoptional
RMS elevation spread; [n_cir]
orientationoptional
Power-weighted mean orientation in Euler angles [bank; tilt; heading]; [3, n_cir]
phioptional
Rotated azimuth angles; [n_cir] vector, each element of length n_path
thetaoptional

calc_cross_polarization_ratio

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Calculate the cross-polarization ratio (XPR) for linear and circular polarization bases

  • Computes aggregate XPR from polarization transfer matrices using the total-power-ratio method: co-pol and cross-pol powers are summed across all qualifying paths per CIR, and XPR is their ratio.
  • XPR is computed in both the linear V/H basis and the circular LHCP/RHCP basis.
  • LOS paths are identified by comparing path length against direct TX-RX distance dTR; paths with path_length <= dTR + window_size are excluded by default (include_los = false).
  • Polarization transfer matrix M is the 2x2 Jones matrix (rows = RX polarisation V/H, columns = TX polarisation V/H), stored column-major with interleaved real/imaginary parts, 8 rows per path: rows 0-1 = (V rx, V tx), rows 2-3 = (H rx, V tx), rows 4-5 = (V rx, H tx), rows 6-7 = (H rx, H tx). Below, M_<rx><tx> names an entry by its receive and transmit polarisation: M_vv = rows 0-1, M_hv = rows 2-3, M_vh = rows 4-5, M_hh = rows 6-7
  • V-XPR and H-XPR are ratios per receive polarisation: V-XPR is the power received in V from V transmission over the power received in V from H transmission; H-XPR likewise for the H receive polarisation
  • The circular entries couple circular patterns through M as get_channels_spherical couples antenna patterns, c(r, t) = r^T M t (plain transpose), with the same circular vectors at both ends, each in that antenna's own (e_theta, e_phi) frame: L = (V, H) = (1, +j) / sqrt(2) (LHCP), R = (1, -j) / sqrt(2) (RHCP). The names follow the IEEE definition (rotation seen along the propagation direction) for the time convention exp(+j 2 pi f t), which the library's coefficients exp(-j 2 pi f tau) imply, and e_theta x e_phi = the outward direction of the pattern. M_<rx><tx>: M_LL = (M_vv - M_hh + j(M_vh + M_hv)) / 2, M_RR = (M_vv - M_hh - j(M_vh + M_hv)) / 2, M_LR = (M_vv + M_hh + j(M_hv - M_vh)) / 2 (receive L, transmit R), M_RL = (M_vv + M_hh + j(M_vh - M_hv)) / 2. Co-polar means the same circular vector at both ends: the LOS matrix diag(1, -1) of get_channels_spherical is co-polar (handedness kept), diag(1, 1) (one mirrored component, as by a single reflection) is cross-polar.
  • LHCP-XPR and RHCP-XPR are ratios per receive polarisation, like V-XPR and H-XPR.
  • Normalization of M does not affect XPR (cancels in ratio) but does affect pg.
  • If cross-pol power is zero and co-pol is positive, XPR is set to infinity; if both are zero, XPR is set to 0.
  • TX/RX positions may be fixed [3, 1] or mobile [3, n_cir].

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::calc_cross_polarization_ratio(
    const std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> &powers,
    const std::vector<arma::Mat<dtype>> &M,
    const std::vector<arma::Col<dtype>> &path_length,
    const arma::Mat<dtype> &tx_pos,
    const arma::Mat<dtype> &rx_pos,
    arma::Mat<dtype> *xpr = nullptr,
    arma::Col<dtype> *pg = nullptr,
    bool include_los = false,
    dtype window_size = 0.01);

Inputs

powers
Path powers in [W]; [n_cir] vector, each element of length n_path
M
Polarization transfer matrices; [n_cir] vector, each element of size [8, n_path]
path_length
Absolute TX-to-RX path lengths; same structure as powers
tx_pos
Transmitter position [x; y; z]; [3, 1] or [3, n_cir]
rx_pos
Receiver position [x; y; z]; [3, 1] or [3, n_cir]
include_losoptional
If true, includes LOS and near-LOS paths in the XPR calculation
window_sizeoptional
LOS exclusion window; paths with path_length <= dTR + window_size are excluded when include_los = false

Outputs

xproptional
XPR on linear scale; [n_cir, 6]; columns:
Col Description
0 Aggregate linear XPR (total V+H co-pol / total V+H cross-pol)
1 V-XPR: sum(abs(M_vv)^2) / sum(abs(M_vh)^2) (receive V)
2 H-XPR: sum(abs(M_hh)^2) / sum(abs(M_hv)^2) (receive H)
3 Aggregate circular XPR (total L+R co-pol / total L+R cross-pol)
4 LHCP XPR: sum(abs(M_LL)^2) / sum(abs(M_LR)^2) (receive L)
5 RHCP XPR: sum(abs(M_RR)^2) / sum(abs(M_RL)^2) (receive R)
pgoptional
Total path gain summed over all paths (including LOS) as 0.5 * sum(powers * (abs(M_vv)^2 + abs(M_hv)^2 + abs(M_vh)^2 + abs(M_hh)^2)); [n_cir]

calc_delay_spread

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Calculates RMS delay spread from per-CIR delays and linear-scale powers

  • Paths with power below p_max / 10^(0.1 * threshold) are excluded; default threshold of 100 dB effectively includes all paths.
  • When granularity > 0, paths falling into the same delay bin of width granularity have their powers summed before computing the spread; function recurses on the binned profile. The bins are placed on a grid common to all CIRs; only occupied bins are stored, so memory does not grow with the delay span. All delays must then be finite, and the global delay span divided by granularity must be below 2^53.

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Calculate the Rician K-Factor from channel impulse response data

  • KF = LOS power / NLOS power; LOS paths are those with length ≤ dTR + window_size, where dTR is the direct TX-RX distance.

Geometry-based stochastic model

A geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) generates channels from statistics of a type of environment, the scenario (e.g. urban macro-cell with or without line of sight), instead of from the geometry of one site. The functions of this section implement the model of 3GPP TR 38.901, clause 7.5 steps 1 to 7: path loss, shadow fading, LOS probability, O2I penetration loss, the large-scale parameters (LSPs) of each link, i.e. the spreads of delays and angles, the K-factor and the cross-polarization ratio, and the clusters.

The statistics of a scenario are read from a conf file by conf_file_read. The folder data/config holds 23 files for TR 38.901 v19.5.0; scenpar_validate completes a parameter set from another source, conf_file_list finds the files and conf_file_write writes them.

Per drop (layout): o2i_loss gives the penetration loss and the indoor distance of each indoor UT; then los_probability evaluates the LOS probability at the outdoor distance d2D - d2D-in. The caller draws the LOS state and the indoor state with sos_rand / sos_randn at the decorrelation distances of the keys LOS_state_lambda and IO_state_lambda, and the O2I variables at the distances of TR 38.901 clause 7.6.3.3 (see o2i_loss). The two state distances apply to all links of a scenario and are stated once in the TR 38.901 files: LOS_state_lambda in the NLOS file, IO_state_lambda in the O2I files; 0 in the other files means "not stated here". Per BS site and scenario (builder): lsf_init_phases draws the random phases once; lsf_draw evaluates them at the links (columns 0 DS, 1 KF, 2 SF, 3 ASD, 4 ASA, 5 ESD, 6 ESA, 7 XPR, 8 absolute TOA: Normal; 9 ground permittivity, 10 UMa environment height: Uniform; each at the decorrelation distance of its key); path_loss returns the path loss and the SF standard deviation; lsp_generate turns the random values into the LSPs of each link and frequency.

The small-scale part (clause 7.5 steps 5 to 7, cluster level): ssf_init_phases draws the phases of the cluster random values per site, scenario and frequency from the LSF seed, ssf_draw evaluates them at the links, and ssf_clusters turns the LSPs and random values into cluster delays, powers and angles with the method 38.901 (clause 7.5), 38.901_MF (clause 7.6.5.1) or quadriga (spatially consistent, frequency-independent). The ray level (steps 8 to 12) follows in a later version.

Where TR 38.901 and QuaDRiGa differ, the TR behaviour is the default; QuaDRiGa's behaviour is available through an argument where it is still wanted (3D correlation, symmetric square root of the LSP cross-correlation matrix, no clipping of the spreads, outdoor path-loss distance of O2I links). Where QuaDRiGa's behaviour was an error, only the corrected rule is implemented.

Units: positions in m, frequencies in Hz, path loss in dB, DS in s, KF, SF and XPR as linear power ratios, angular spreads in degrees.

conf_file_list

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

List the scenarios defined by the conf files in a set of directories

  • Lists the regular files and symbolic links to regular files whose name ends in .conf (case-sensitive) and is longer than .conf, not recursive. The scenario name is the file name without this extension, whatever characters it has.
  • Directories are processed in the given order, the files of one directory in byte-wise sorted order of their names (digits before upper case before lower case)
  • A file whose name was already found in an earlier directory is skipped completely, so the first directory wins. This allows a local folder to override the files of a shared folder.
  • With parse_shortnames = true each file is read and one entry is added right after the file for every line ShortName = name that is not a comment. Other lines are not examined; a UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is skipped.
  • Throws std::invalid_argument if a short name equals an earlier entry, if a file name equals an earlier short name, or if the value of a ShortName line is not one name of the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _
  • Throws std::runtime_error if a listed file cannot be opened for reading the short names
  • A directory that does not exist, is not a directory or cannot be listed is skipped; an empty string is the current directory
  • A failed call leaves the outputs untouched

Declaration

arma::uword quadriga_lib::conf_file_list(
    const std::vector<std::string> &dirs,
    std::vector<std::string> &scenarios,
    std::vector<std::string> *file_names = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *file_dirs = nullptr,
    bool parse_shortnames = true);

Inputs

dirs
Directories, searched in this order; can be empty
parse_shortnamesoptional
true: read the files and add their short names; false: list the files only, which is faster

scenarios
Scenario names and short names; previous content is discarded; [n_scen]
file_namesoptional
File name including .conf for each entry; [n_scen]
file_dirsoptional
Directory of the file for each entry, exactly as given in dirs; [n_scen]

conf_file_read

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Read and validate a QuaDRiGa scenario configuration file

  • A conf file is a text file with one Key = value assignment per line; % starts a comment; blank lines are allowed; line ends can be LF or CRLF; space and tab are white space; a UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is skipped
  • Keys are case-sensitive names of the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _; there are four kinds:
    • Scenario parameters: n_key = 171 numeric keys with one number each, returned in scenpar. Keys that are not in the file have their default value. The names and their order are returned in key_order.
    • SubpathMethod: one of the words legacy, Laplacian, mmMAGIC; default legacy
    • Path-loss parameters: every key that starts with PL_. PL_model has one name as value. All others have one or more numbers separated by white space and are returned in plpar without the prefix.
    • ShortName: an alias for the scenario, one name; can occur several times with different values
  • Any other key is ignored and reported in ignored_keys; its value is not examined
  • A key that is stated more than once has its last value
  • Numbers are decimal with an optional sign, an optional decimal point and an optional exponent (e or E), for example -6.28, .5, 6.2e-07; Inf, +Inf and -Inf are accepted in any case
  • A number beyond the range of a double (1e400) is an error "out of range"; a number below the smallest subnormal reads as 0 (or -0)
  • Numbers are read independent of the global locale (the decimal point is always .)
  • Elevation angles are used throughout (+90 deg is up); no key refers to a zenith angle
  • The 171 keys are 138 numeric keys of QuaDRiGa and 33 keys for 3GPP TR 38.901 v19.5.0. With their default of 0 the new keys have no effect.
  • The QuaDRiGa key GR_epsilon (fixed relative permittivity of the ground) is not supported and is reported in ignored_keys like any other unknown key; the permittivity is complex and is set in the simulation
  • The 28 correlation keys (asD_ds to xpr_esa) define the symmetric matrix lsp_xcorr with unit diagonal
  • Throws std::runtime_error if the file cannot be opened or is a directory
  • Throws std::invalid_argument with file name and line number for a line that is not blank, not a comment and not a well-formed assignment: no =, more or less than one name before the =, a missing value, a word where a number is required or the reverse, a second value or other text after the value, NaN, complex numbers, a number out of range, a PL_ key without a name, a ShortName value stated twice
  • With validate = true, a value that fails the checks of scenpar_validate is an error as well
  • A correlation matrix that is not positive definite is not an error; it is reported by the return value
  • The file is parsed and checked completely before any output is written; a failed call leaves all outputs untouched

Declaration

bool quadriga_lib::conf_file_read(
    const std::string &fn,
    std::unordered_map<std::string, double> &scenpar,
    std::string *subpath_method = nullptr,
    std::string *pl_model = nullptr,
    std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<double>> *plpar = nullptr,
    arma::mat *lsp_xcorr = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *key_order = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *pl_order = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *short_names = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *ignored_keys = nullptr,
    bool validate = true);

Inputs

Path to the conf file
validateoptional
true: apply the value checks of scenpar_validate; false: only the line grammar is checked

Outputs

scenpar
Numeric scenario parameters; previous content is discarded; n_key = 171 entries
subpath_methodoptional
Value of SubpathMethod; legacy if not in the file
pl_modeloptional
Value of PL_model; empty if not in the file
plparoptional
Path-loss parameters; keys without the prefix PL_; PL_model is not included; empty if the file has no such key; n_pl entries with one or more values each

LSP cross-correlation matrix; order of rows and columns: DS, KF, SF, ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA, XPR; [8, 8]

Canonical order of the keys in scenpar: the QuaDRiGa order without SubpathMethod (its position is between elements 105 and 106, 0-based), then the 33 new keys; [n_key]

conf_file_write

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Write a QuaDRiGa scenario configuration file

  • Writes scenario parameters, path-loss parameters and short names in the layout of the conf files shipped with QuaDRiGa, so that conf_file_read returns the same values bit for bit
  • Header: % Config file for scenario "name" with the file name without the extension .conf, then the reference ref, the validity range and one line ShortName = name per short name
  • Up to 10 sections follow, each with a header and, if the entry of ref_sec is not empty, a line % See: ref; ref_sec. Index in ref_sec and write order:
    • 0: Large scale distributions, with an overview formula per LSP; 1: Large-Scale fading decorrelation distances; 2: Inter-parameter correlations, with the correlation matrix as comment; 3: Model parameters; 8: EoD offset; 4: Decorrelation distance for the small-scale fading spatial consistency; 5: Parameters for the ground reflection extension; 6: Absolute time of arrival offset; 9: Optional modelling components; 7: Path-loss model
    • The indices 0 to 7 are those of QuaDRiGa, so its 8 section references can be passed unchanged
  • Within a section, keys are grouped into paragraphs separated by a blank line; correlations are written in the row order of the matrix, all other keys in the order of key_order; SubpathMethod stands before LOS_scatter_radius
  • The overview formula of an LSP shows its mean and STD with the frequency, distance, height and elevation terms; with LSP_fc_min > 0 the frequency is written as max( fGHz, fc_min ); the ESD line also has the terms of ES_D_mu_A to ES_D_mu_D and, if ES_D_mu_min is not -Inf, the lower limit of the mean; the DS line has the term log10( a · V/S + b ) when DS_VS > 0 (a = DS_VS_a, b = DS_VS_b; V/S stays symbolic)
  • Each line is name = value % comment, with the name padded to 19 and the value to 13 characters. The comment states the unit; for the mean and STD of an LSP it adds the reference point of the frequency, distance, height and elevation terms, e.g. @ 1 GHz.
  • The path-loss section has the formula blocks of the model (logdist, dual_slope, nlos, tripple_slope), the line PL_model, then the keys of plpar with the prefix PL_; known keys have a comment that can depend on the model; several values of one key are separated by a space
  • Numbers are written with up to 15 significant digits, or with 16 or 17 where 15 do not read back to the same double in conf_file_read, independent of the global locale; Inf and -Inf are written as such, -0 is kept
  • With write_defaults = false a key is written only if its value differs from the default, compared bit for bit; SubpathMethod only if it is not legacy; a section without a written key is left out
  • With write_defaults = true all 171 keys and SubpathMethod are written
  • Validation before the file is opened: the file name has no line break; the value checks of scenpar_validate (unknown keys, NaN, classes, subpath_method); pl_model empty or one name; plpar keys are names other than model, each with at least one value and no NaN; pl_order names each key of plpar once; short names are names and distinct; ref and ref_sec have no line break; ref_sec has at most 10 entries; valid_range is empty or [4, 2]
  • The text is written to a temporary file in the same directory, which must be writable, and then renamed to fn; a symbolic link fn is written through
  • A failed call does not create a file and leaves an existing file unchanged; an existing file is replaced and keeps its permissions
  • Throws std::invalid_argument for invalid input; std::runtime_error if the file cannot be opened or written, or if fn exists and is not a regular file that can be opened for writing
  • Every file written passes conf_file_read with validate = true and without ignored keys

Declaration

    const std::string &pl_model = "",
    const std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<double>> *plpar = nullptr,
    const std::vector<std::string> *pl_order = nullptr,
    const std::vector<std::string> *short_names = nullptr,
    const std::string &ref = "",
    const std::vector<std::string> *ref_sec = nullptr,
    const arma::mat *valid_range = nullptr,
    bool write_defaults = false);

Inputs

Path of the conf file to write
scenpar
Numeric scenario parameters; any subset of the n_key = 171 keys of conf_file_read; missing keys have their default
subpath_methodoptional

true: write all keys; false: write only keys that differ from their default

los_probability

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

LOS probability of a set of links, TR 38.901 Table 7.4.2-1 and other named models

  • Evaluates the probability that a link is in line-of-sight (LOS) for each link, from its 2D distance and the BS and UT heights, and optionally the soft LOS state of TR 38.901 eq. (7.6-18)
  • Notation: d = d2d_out(l), hB = h_bs(l), hU = h_ut(l) in m, lg = log10, ln the natural logarithm. All results are limited to [0, 1]
  • TR 38.901 v19.5.0 Table 7.4.2-1:
    • 38.901_RMa: 1 for d <= 10, else exp(-(d - 10)/1000)
    • 38.901_UMi: 1 for d <= 18, else 18/d + exp(-d/36)·(1 - 18/d)
    • 38.901_UMa: 1 for d <= 18, else (18/d + exp(-d/63)·(1 - 18/d))·(1 + C'·5/4·(d/100)³·exp(-d/150)) with C' = 0 for hU <= 13, ((hU - 13)/10)^1.5 for 13 < hU <= 23 and 1 for hU > 23; for hU > 13 the formula exceeds 1 slightly just above 18 m (e.g. up to 1.0060 for hU = 22.5), where the limit gives 1
    • 38.901_InH_Mixed (mixed office): 1 for d <= 1.2, exp(-(d - 1.2)/4.7) for 1.2 < d < 6.5, exp(-(d - 6.5)/32.6)·0.32 for d >= 6.5
    • 38.901_InH_Open (open office): 1 for d <= 5, exp(-(d - 5)/70.8) for 5 < d <= 49, exp(-(d - 49)/211.7)·0.54 for d > 49
    • 38.901_InF_SL, 38.901_InF_DL: exp(-d·kinv) with kinv = -ln(1 - r)/d_clutter
    • 38.901_InF_SH, 38.901_InF_DH: with kinv = -ln(1 - r)/d_clutter: 1 for hU >= h_c (UT above the clutter); exp(-d·kinv·(h_c - hU)/(hB - hU)) for hB > hU (TR: k = -d_clutter/ln(1 - r)·(hB - hU)/(h_c - hU)); exp(-d·kinv) (the rule of SL and DL) for hB <= hU < h_c, where the TR formula has a BS above the UT and would give k <= 0. r = 0 gives 1
    • 38.901_InF_HH: 1
    • 38.901_SMa (TR v19): 1 for d <= 10 or hB <= hU, else exp(-d·(k_com + k_res + k_veg)) with k_x = -ln(1 - r_x)/d_clutter·max(h_x - hU, 0)/(hB - hU), heights h_com = 20, h_res = 8, h_veg = 15 m, densities r_com = 0.02, r_res = 0.18, r_veg = r_clutter; the TR writes max(., 0) only for the residential term, which gives the same values for hU < 15 m (the TR range)
  • Defaults of the clutter arguments (NaN), TR 38.901 Table 7.2-4 and Table 7.8-7 for InF, Table 7.4.2-1 for SMa:
    • InF_SL: r = 0.2, d_clutter = 10 m; InF_DL: r = 0.6, d_clutter = 2 m
    • InF_SH: r = 0.2, d_clutter = 10 m, h_c = 2 m; InF_DH: r = 0.6, d_clutter = 2 m, h_c = 6 m
    • SMa: d_clutter = 30 m, r_veg = 0 (no vegetation; 0.1 sparse, 0.2 dense vegetation); h_clutter is not used
    • The other models ignore the clutter arguments (they are validated for every model)
  • TR 38.811 (via QuaDRiGa), 38.811_DenseUrban, 38.811_Urban, 38.811_Suburban, 38.811_Rural: the LOS probability in percent over the elevation atan2(hB, d) in degrees (absolute BS height), linear interpolation over the grid -90, 0, 10, ..., 90 deg, times 0.01:
    • DenseUrban: 0, 0, 28.2, 33.1, 39.8, 46.8, 53.7, 61.2, 73.8, 82.0, 98.1
    • Urban: 0, 0, 24.6, 38.6, 49.3, 61.3, 72.6, 80.5, 91.9, 96.8, 99.2
    • Suburban and Rural: 0, 0, 78.2, 86.9, 91.9, 92.9, 93.5, 94.0, 94.9, 95.2, 99.8
  • QuaDRiGa, QuaDRiGa_Industrial: min(1, exp(-(d + 20)/80)·exp(min(hB, 8)/5 - 1))
  • LOS: 1, NLOS: 0
  • Soft LOS state (TR 38.901 eq. 7.6-18), computed when los_soft is requested: los_soft(l, k) = 1/2 + atan(sqrt(20/lambda_k)·(rnd_g(l) + F(p_los(l))))/pi, lambda_k = c/fc(k) with c = 299792458 m/s and F(p) = sqrt(2)·erfinv(2p - 1) the inverse of the standard normal CDF (accurate to 1e-10·max(1, abs(F)) for p in [1e-12, 1 - 1e-12]). p = 1 gives 1, p = 0 gives 0. los_soft > 0.5 exactly when rnd_g > -F(p), which has the probability p for rnd_g from N(0,1)
  • The LOS state itself (a draw against p_los) and its spatial correlation are the caller's: e.g. a spatially consistent uniform value from sos_rand, or rnd_g from sos_randn, at the decorrelation distance of the scenario key LOS_state_lambda (TR 38.901 Table 7.6.3.1-2). The key applies to all links of a scenario and is stated only in its NLOS conf file (0 in the LOS and O2I files means "not stated here"). The LOS_state_lambda of the InF conf files is d_clutter / 2 of the TR defaults; it does not follow a d_clutter argument, so a caller who changes d_clutter passes its own correlation distance
  • O2I UTs: Table 7.4.2-1 uses the outdoor distance d2d_out = d2D - d2D-in with d2D-in from o2i_loss, which therefore runs first; the caller clamps d2d_out at 0 (negative distances are rejected). Indoor scenarios (InH, InF) pass the 2D distance
  • Outputs must not share memory with the inputs or with each other
  • Validation, in this order: the model name; d2d_out finite and >= 0; h_bs and h_ut with 1 or n_link elements and finite; d_clutter NaN or finite and > 0, r_clutter NaN or in [0, 1), h_clutter NaN or finite and >= 0 (for every model); if los_soft is requested: rnd_g and fc present, rnd_g with n_link finite elements, fc non-empty, finite and > 0. Without los_soft, rnd_g and fc are ignored. All checks run before any output is written

Declaration

    const arma::vec &d2d_out,

lsf_draw

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Spatially correlated normalized random values of the large-scale generators at a set of links

  • Evaluates the 11 large-scale fading generators of lsf_init_phases at the links: column 0 DS, 1 KF, 2 SF, 3 ASD, 4 ASA, 5 ESD, 6 ESA, 7 XPR, 8 absolute TOA (Normal(0,1)), 9 ground permittivity, 10 UMa environment height hE (Uniform(0,1)); each generator with the sum-of-sinusoids frequencies of preset at its own decorrelation distance (a distance of 0 is used as 0.1 m)
  • scenpar is completed and validated by scenpar_validate as in lsf_init_phases; its messages pass through unchanged
  • Single mobility (dual_mobility = false): column g is the field of generator g at the Rx position, x_g = s_g(rx) with s_g(x) = sqrt(2/n_coeff) · sum_n cos( 2·pi · f_n·x + phi_n ) and the phases of slice 0; the values do not depend on tx_pos
  • Dual mobility: the Tx is a second device. Its side uses slice 1, i.e. the field of the mirror generator m(g) at the Tx position (ASD and ASA, ESD and ESA exchanged). Self-mirrored generators (DS, KF, SF, XPR, TOA, 9, 10) share one map: x_g = ( s_g(rx) + s_g(tx) ) / sqrt( 2 + 2·A_g(D) ), with the Tx-Rx distance D and the ACF A_g of the preset, linearly interpolated. The pairs are two maps: x_g = ( s_g(rx) + s_m(tx) ) / sqrt(2). Columns 3 to 6 thus stay Normal(0,1), and ASD/ASA and ESD/ESA have the correlation ( A_g(D) + A_m(D) ) / 2 at the Tx-Rx distance, 1 at D = 0 (then the two columns are equal)
  • Swap reciprocity in dual mobility: swapping tx_pos and rx_pos leaves columns 0, 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 10 unchanged and swaps column 3 with 4 and column 5 with 6, exactly (the same evaluations in swapped roles), also for unequal decorrelation distances and with bias-removed phases, when both calls use the same phase cube
  • Uniform columns 9 and 10: 0.5 · erfc( -x / sqrt(2) ) of the Normal value
  • horizontal = true: the positions are projected on the x-y plane (z = 0) and the values do not depend on z; false: 3D positions. D is measured in the same space
  • 2D and 3D mode give the same per-link statistics. In 3D mode the height separates the floors: the LSPs of UTs on different floors are correlated by the ACF of their height difference, while TR 38.901 (Table 7.5-6 note 3) assumes no correlation between floors. floor_id is therefore not accepted with horizontal = false
  • Floors: links with different floor IDs see different fields, links with equal IDs share one field. Floor q adds the offsets 2·pi · k · n / N + psi_b(n) to the phases of all generators on both sides, with N = n_coeff, k = q mod N, b = q div N, n = 0 ... N-1, psi_0 = 0 and psi_b(n) = 2·pi · u_n for b >= 1, where u_n are the uniform numbers of a std::mt19937_64 seeded with b (the upper 53 bits of each raw output times 2^-53). Floor 0 and floor_id = nullptr give the same values
  • Fields of two floors are uncorrelated at equal horizontal positions (TR 38.901 Table 7.5-6 note 3): exactly for two IDs in the same block of N IDs, with a random residual of standard deviation 1/sqrt(2N) for IDs in different blocks (0.044 for 256 sinusoids). At other horizontal lags the cross-correlation of two floors is not zero (up to about 0.16 for 256 sinusoids), the same level as for random offsets. Mirror relations and swap reciprocity hold per floor
  • floor_id is the caller's floor index of the UT: for the UT heights hUT = 3·(n_fl - 1) + 1.5 of TR 38.901 Table 7.2-1 it is n_fl - 1; outdoor UTs use 0
  • Dual mobility with floors: floor_id is one value per link and its offsets are added on both sides, i.e. both devices of a link are on the link's floor. A Tx device on another floor than its Rx (e.g. a D2D link between two floors) is evaluated on the floor of the Rx, so the same Tx device sees different fields on links to Rx devices on different floors
  • The value of a link does not depend on the other links of the call
  • Precision: the sinusoids are evaluated by sos_val with the AVX2 kernel where available (sine and cosine in single precision, accumulation in double); the values deviate from a double-precision evaluation by less than 4e-7 · sqrt(2 · n_coeff) (9e-6 for 256 sinusoids)
  • preset and horizontal must be those of lsf_init_phases. A wrong preset with the same number of sinusoids (e.g. Exp256 for Comb256) cannot be detected
  • n_link = 0 returns rnd with size [0, 11]. rnd may share memory with tx_pos or rx_pos (the positions are copied before rnd is written)
  • Validation order: positions (3 columns, rows of tx_pos, finite values), preset, scenpar, size of phase, finite phase, length of floor_id, floor_id with horizontal = false

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::lsf_draw(

    const arma::cube &phase,
    const arma::mat &tx_pos,
    const arma::mat &rx_pos,
    arma::mat &rnd,
    const arma::uvec *floor_id = nullptr,
    bool dual_mobility = false,
    const std::string &preset = "Comb256",
    bool horizontal = true);

Inputs

Scenario parameters as returned by conf_file_read or scenpar_validate; missing keys have their default value; only the 10 decorrelation distances are used

Phases in [rad] from lsf_init_phases; slice 0 = Rx side, slice 1 = Tx side; must be finite; [n_coeff, 11, 2], n_coeff of preset

true: Tx and Rx both move, the Tx side is evaluated as a second device

horizontaloptional
true: 2D correlation in the x-y plane (TR 38.901 behaviour); false: 3D correlation (legacy QuaDRiGa behaviour); must match lsf_init_phases

Output

rnd
Random values; columns 0 to 8 Normal(0,1), columns 9 and 10 Uniform(0,1); [n_link, 11]

lsf_init_phases

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Draw the random phases of the large-scale generators of one BS site and scenario

  • The large-scale fading (LSF) of a site is described by 11 spatially correlated sum-of-sinusoids generators, one column each: 0 DS, 1 KF, 2 SF, 3 ASD, 4 ASA, 5 ESD, 6 ESA, 7 XPR, 8 absolute TOA (Normal fields), 9 ground permittivity, 10 UMa environment height hE (Uniform fields). Their decorrelation distances are the scenario parameters DS_lambda, KF_lambda, SF_lambda, AS_D_lambda, AS_A_lambda, ES_D_lambda, ES_A_lambda, XPR_lambda, absTOA_lambda, SC_lambda and again SF_lambda for hE; a decorrelation distance of 0 is used as 0.1 m. The generator of column 8 exists also when the absolute TOA is disabled
  • This function draws the phases; lsf_draw evaluates them at the links. The caller stores phase and evaluates the same fields again along tracks or on maps
  • scenpar is completed with the defaults of missing keys and validated by scenpar_validate; its messages (e.g. for an unknown key or a negative decorrelation distance) pass through unchanged. An invalid value of a key that is not used here throws as well
  • Slice 0 (Rx side) holds the phases of the 11 generators. Without bias removal it equals sos_init_phases(n_coeff, 11, seed) of sos_init_phases, with n_coeff the number of sinusoids of preset. The same seed gives the same phases
  • Slice 1 (Tx side) is always the mirror of slice 0: slice1.col(g) = slice0.col(m(g)) with the mirror generator m(g): ASD and ASA (3, 4) and ESD and ESA (5, 6) are exchanged, all others mirror themselves. For dual mobility the departure spreads at the Tx are thus the arrival spreads of the Tx as a second device
  • Bias removal (remove_bias = true, rx_pos given, n_link > 2): one realisation of a correlated field has a non-zero mean over a drop. For each Normal generator (columns 0 to 8) one common phase offset is applied with sos_remove_bias, so that the sample mean of its field over the positions is exactly 0. Single mobility: over the Rx positions; tx_pos is not used. Dual mobility: over the Rx and Tx positions together (2·n_link positions), because the field of a generator is shared by both devices (the Tx side of ASD is the ASA field); tx_pos is then required. The Uniform generators 9 and 10 are never corrected
  • The correction is applied to slice 0 and the Tx side is mirrored afterwards, so the mirror relation holds exactly with and without bias removal. Swapping tx_pos and rx_pos in dual mobility gives the same phases up to rounding (the sums over the positions are formed in another order)
  • Consequences for lsf_draw at the same positions: in single mobility the link mean of columns 0 to 8 is 0; in dual mobility the link mean of DS, KF, SF, XPR and TOA is 0 when all links have the same Tx-Rx distance (the normalisation is then the same for all links), while ASD/ASA and ESD/ESA have a zero link mean only approximately (their two devices see different fields, each corrected over the union of the positions)
  • The positions are used as in lsf_draw: projected on the x-y plane (z = 0) for horizontal = true, in 3D for horizontal = false. preset and horizontal must be the same in lsf_draw
  • 2D mode: all positions in rx_pos are treated as one field (floor 0): one phase correction per generator cannot zero the means of several floor fields at once. For a drop with UTs on several floors pass the positions of one floor (e.g. the links of floor 0) or set remove_bias = false; the fields of the other floors keep their sample mean. 3D mode (horizontal = false): there are no floor IDs (the height separates the floors) and the correction covers all given positions as one 3D field
  • 2D and 3D mode give the same per-link statistics. In 3D mode the LSPs of UTs on different floors are correlated by the ACF of their height difference, while TR 38.901 (Table 7.5-6 note 3) assumes no correlation between floors
  • The correction removes variance: the field is conditioned on a zero mean over the positions, which costs little only when the positions spread over many decorrelation distances (see sos_remove_bias)
  • With fewer than 3 positions, without rx_pos or with remove_bias = false no correction is made
  • TR 38.901 clause 7.4.4 literally (exponential ACF, no bias removal): preset = "Exp256" and remove_bias = false; the defaults Comb256 and the bias removal are QuaDRiGa choices
  • Reason for Comb256: the TR gives the exponential ACF (eq. 7.4-5) as a fit "with sufficient accuracy", not as an exact requirement; its kink at zero distance makes the values evolve roughly along a track. Comb256 (Gaussian near zero, exponential tail, same decorrelation distance) evolves smoothly
  • phase must not share memory with tx_pos or rx_pos
  • Validation order: seed, preset, scenpar, then the positions (3 columns, rows of tx_pos 1 or n_link when both are given, finite values), then the requirement of tx_pos for the bias removal in dual mobility

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::lsf_init_phases(
    const std::unordered_map<std::string, double> &scenpar,
    arma::cube &phase,
    arma::sword seed = -1,
    const arma::mat *tx_pos = nullptr,
    const arma::mat *rx_pos = nullptr,
    bool dual_mobility = false,
    bool remove_bias = true,
    const std::string &preset = "Comb256",
    bool horizontal = true);

Inputs

scenpar
Scenario parameters as returned by conf_file_read or scenpar_validate; missing keys have their default value; only the 10 decorrelation distances are used
seedoptional
Seed of the random phases, must be >= -1; -1 = system random device, a new set of phases on each call
tx_posoptional
Tx positions in [m]; used only for the bias removal with dual mobility, required there; one row is used for all links; [1, 3] or [n_link, 3]
rx_posoptional
Rx positions of the drop in [m] (one floor in 2D mode, all floors in 3D mode) for the bias removal; omitted or fewer than 3 rows = no bias removal; [n_link, 3]
dual_mobilityoptional
true: Tx and Rx both move, the Tx is a second device on the same maps
remove_biasoptional
true: remove the sample mean of the Normal fields over the positions
presetoptional
Sum-of-sinusoids preset, see sos_preset; sets n_coeff
horizontaloptional
true: 2D correlation in the x-y plane (TR 38.901 behaviour); false: 3D correlation (legacy QuaDRiGa behaviour)

Output

phase
Phases in [rad]; slice 0 = Rx side, slice 1 = Tx side (mirror of slice 0); all values in [-pi, pi); [n_coeff, 11, 2]

  • ssf_init_phases (the small-scale sets, seeds derived from this seed)
  • sos_init_phases (the raw phases)
  • sos_remove_bias (the bias removal of one generator)

lsp_generate

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Large-scale parameters of a set of links from normalized random values

  • Generates the 8 large-scale parameters (LSPs) of TR 38.901 clause 7.5 step 4 per link and frequency: delay spread DS, Ricean K-factor KF, shadow fading SF, azimuth spreads of departure and arrival ASD, ASA, elevation spreads of departure and arrival ESD, ESA and cross-polarization ratio XPR. The random values rnd are the normalized, spatially correlated values of lsf_draw (columns 0 to 7 Normal(0,1) for the 8 LSPs, column 8 Normal(0,1) for the absolute TOA, column 9 Uniform(0,1) for the ground permittivity; column 10 is not used here)
  • scenpar is completed with the defaults of missing keys and validated by scenpar_validate; its messages pass through unchanged. An invalid value of a key that is not used here throws as well
  • Mean and standard deviation in the log domain, per link l and frequency k, with the key prefix P of the LSP (DS, KF, SF, AS_D, AS_A, ES_D, ES_A, XPR), the 2D distance d2D, the Tx height hBS = tx_pos.z and the Rx height hUT = rx_pos.z: d = max(d2D, 1e-4), h = max(hBS, 1e-4), a = atan(h / d) (elevation in rad), f' = max(fc / 1e9, LSP_fc_min) (frequency in GHz, limited from below by LSP_fc_min for all LSP terms); mu = P_mu + P_gamma·lg(P_omega + f') + P_epsilon·lg(d) + P_zeta·lg(h) + P_alpha·lg(a); s = max(0, P_sigma + P_delta·lg(P_omega + f')); sigma = max(0, s + P_kappa·lg(d) + P_tau·lg(h) + P_beta·lg(a)). The standard deviation is limited at 0 after all terms, since a negative value would flip the sign of the realization and its cross-correlations. SF has no mean keys (mean 0). A frequency term with the coefficient 0 contributes 0; an active one (P_gamma or P_delta not 0) requires P_omega + f' > 0 at every frequency. The multiplying coefficients (P_sigma, P_gamma, P_delta, P_epsilon, P_zeta, P_alpha, P_kappa, P_tau, P_beta, ES_D_mu_A to ES_D_mu_D, P_omega of an active frequency term) must be finite; P_mu and ES_D_mu_min may be infinite
  • DS with the V/S term of TR 38.901 Table 7.5-6 Part-3 (InF): if DS_VS > 0, mu += lg(DS_VS_a·DS_VS + DS_VS_b). The InF files set DS_VS for the hall of their calibration scenario; a caller with another hall sets DS_VS (V/S in m) in its copy of scenpar
  • ESD with the terms of TR 38.901 Tables 7.5-7 to 7.5-12: mu += ES_D_mu_A·d/1000 + ES_D_mu_B·hUT + ES_D_mu_C·abs(hUT - h) + ES_D_mu_D·max(hUT - h, 0), then the floor mu = max(mu, ES_D_mu_min)
  • Units of mean and std: DS in lg(s); ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA in lg(deg); KF, SF and XPR in dB
  • sf_sigma (e.g. from the path-loss model) replaces the SF standard deviation per link and frequency, also in lsp_sigma; it must be finite and >= 0 (a negative value would flip the sign of the shadow fading)
  • Cross-correlation: x = Q·s with s = rnd(l, 0..7) and a root Q of the LSP cross-correlation matrix R of scenpar (Q·Q^T = R). cholesky = true (TR 38.901 clause 7.5 step 4): Cholesky factorization in the TR order [SF, KF, DS, ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA], XPR appended last; the SF value is passed through (x_SF = s_SF). cholesky = false: the symmetric square root of R (principal root, legacy QuaDRiGa behaviour); it does not depend on the order of the parameters. Both throw if R is not positive definite
  • The same x is used for all frequencies of a link (TR 38.901 clause 7.6.5)
  • Linear values: lsp = 10^(mu + sigma·x) for DS, ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA; 10^(0.1·(mu + sigma·x)) for KF, SF, XPR. clip_spreads = true (TR 38.901 clause 7.5 step 4): ASD and ASA are limited to 104 deg, ESD and ESA to 52 deg; lsp_mu and lsp_sigma are not affected
  • rnd = zeros(n_link, 11) gives the median LSPs; lsp_mu and lsp_sigma are the mean and std without any randomness
  • Absolute TOA offset (TR 38.901 clause 7.6.9): active if absTOA_mu > -30, then abs_toa = min(10^(absTOA_mu + absTOA_sigma·rnd(l, 8)), 2·absTOA_Lmax / c) with c = 299792458 m/s, without the bound if absTOA_Lmax = 0 (absTOA_sigma must be finite); 0 if not active. The InF and InH NLOS files set absTOA_Lmax to the largest dimension of the hall or office of their calibration scenario; a caller with another hall sets the key; in the TR 38.901 files the offset is active in all NLOS and O2I files (an O2I link has no LOS ray) and off in the LOS files
  • Ground permittivity with U = rnd(l, 9) and f = fc / 1e9 (not limited by LSP_fc_min): dry ground 3 + j·0.003·f^1.34, medium 30.4·f^-0.47 + j·0.18·f^1.05, wet 31.3·f^-0.48 + j·0.63·f^0.77; linear interpolation from dry (U = 0) to medium (U = 0.5) to wet (U = 1). The imaginary part is >= 0; TR 38.901 eq. (7.6-40) writes the complex permittivity with the opposite sign of the imaginary part, so the TR reflection formulas take the complex conjugate gr_eps_re - j·gr_eps_im. Column 9 of rnd must be in [0, 1] when gr_eps_re or gr_eps_im is requested; it is not checked otherwise
  • The three ground types are QuaDRiGa's fits (as in QuaDRiGa's gen_lsf_parameters), not the models of TR 38.901 Table 7.6.8-1: very dry ground agrees, medium and wet ground differ (e.g. at 3.5 GHz medium 16.87 + j·0.67 here, 13.23 + j·1.39 for medium dry ground of the table; wet j·1.65 vs. j·3.93). A caller who needs the table values computes them with eq. (7.6-40) to (7.6-42)
  • EoD offset in degrees, positive = up (the negative of the ZOD offset of TR 38.901 Tables 7.5-7 to 7.5-12), with f', d, h as above: e = EoD_offset_e + EoD_offset_e_gamma·lg f'; if EoD_offset_b > 0: e += 10^((EoD_offset_a + EoD_offset_a_gamma·lg f')·lg(max(EoD_offset_b, d)) + EoD_offset_c + EoD_offset_c_gamma·lg f' + EoD_offset_c_hUT·hUT); if EoD_offset_hcl > 0 and hUT < EoD_offset_hcl: e += (atan((EoD_offset_hcl - h)/d) - atan((hUT - h)/d))·180/pi. The coefficients EoD_offset_e, _e_gamma, _a, _a_gamma, _c, _c_gamma, _c_hUT must be finite
  • Optional outputs that are not requested are not computed. n_link = 0 gives outputs with 0 rows
  • Outputs must not share memory with the inputs or with each other
  • Validation order: positions, fc, rnd, sf_sigma, scenpar, positive definiteness, column 9 of rnd, the coefficients and frequency terms of the 8 LSPs, the EoD_offset_ coefficients (if eod_offset_deg is requested) and absTOA_sigma (if abs_toa is requested and active) finite; all checks run before any output is written

Declaration

void quadriga_lib::lsp_generate(
    const std::unordered_map<std::string, double> &scenpar,

    const arma::mat &tx_pos,

    arma::cube &lsp,
    const arma::mat *sf_sigma = nullptr,
    arma::vec *abs_toa = nullptr,

Inputs

scenpar
Scenario parameters as returned by conf_file_read or scenpar_validate; missing keys have their default value; the LSP cross-correlation matrix must be positive definite
fc
Carrier frequencies in [Hz], finite and > 0; [n_freq]
tx_pos
Tx positions in [m]; one row is used for all links; [1, 3] or [n_link, 3]

SF standard deviation in [dB], finite and >= 0; replaces the value from scenpar; omitted = the scenario value; [n_link, n_freq]

true: Cholesky root in the TR order; false: symmetric square root (legacy)

true: limit ASD and ASA to 104 deg, ESD and ESA to 52 deg

Outputs

Large-scale parameters; slices: 0 DS in [s], 1 KF (linear), 2 SF (linear power ratio), 3 ASD, 4 ASA, 5 ESD, 6 ESA in [deg], 7 XPR (linear); [n_link, n_freq, 8]
abs_toaoptional
Absolute TOA offset in [s], 0 if disabled; [n_link]

Mean in the log domain (lg for DS, ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA; dB for KF, SF, XPR); [n_link, n_freq, 8]
lsp_sigmaoptional

o2i_loss

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

O2I building or car penetration loss of a set of UTs, TR 38.901 clause 7.4.3

  • Draws for each UT one of the given penetration-loss models and evaluates its loss at each carrier frequency, from four normalized random values per UT; f = fc / 1e9 in GHz, lg = log10
  • Material losses of TR 38.901 v19.5.0 Table 7.4.3-1 in dB: L_glass = 2 + 0.2 f, L_IRR = 25.4 + 0.11 f (IRR glass, Release 19 value), L_concrete = 5 + 4 f, L_plywood = 1.03 + 0.17 f; external wall tw(p1, L1, p2, L2) = 5 - 10·lg(p1·10^(-L1/10) + p2·10^(-L2/10))
  • Models, with N = rnd(u, 3) and the indoor 2D distance d2din:
    • low (low-loss, Table 7.4.3-2): tw(0.3, L_glass, 0.7, L_concrete) + 0.5·d2din + 4.4·N
    • high (high-loss, Table 7.4.3-2): tw(0.7, L_IRR, 0.3, L_concrete) + 0.5·d2din + 6.5·N
    • low_A (low-loss A, Table 7.4.3-2): tw(0.3, L_glass, 0.7, L_plywood) + 0.5·d2din + 4.4·N
    • legacy_6GHz (backward compatible model for single-frequency simulations below 6 GHz, Table 7.4.3-3): 20 + 0.5·d2din, no deviation; it goes with a shadow-fading std of 7 dB (the O2I conf files of UMa and UMi have SF_sigma = 7)
    • car (clause 7.4.3.2): 9 + 5·N; car_metal (metallized car windows): 20 + 5·N; no indoor distance
  • Columns of rnd: 0 = Uniform(0,1) for the model choice, 1 and 2 = Uniform(0,1) for the indoor distance, 3 = Normal(0,1) for the deviation (sigma_P of Table 7.4.3-2, the car loss)
  • Model choice per UT: Ccum_j = (w_0 + ... + w_j)/sum(w); the model is the smallest j with rnd(u, 0) < Ccum_j, or, if there is none, the last j with w_j > 0. A model with weight 0 is never chosen
  • Indoor distance: low, high, low_A: d2din = min(rnd(u, 1), rnd(u, 2))·d2d_in_max, the minimum of two uniforms of clause 7.4.3.1; legacy_6GHz: d2din = rnd(u, 1)·d2d_in_max (one uniform, Table 7.4.3-3); car, car_metal: 0
  • The caller draws rnd with sos_rand and sos_randn at the correlation distances of TR 38.901 clause 7.6.3.3 (building type 50 m for column 0, d2D-in 25 m for columns 1 and 2, sigma_P 10 m for column 3) and adds loss to the path loss of the indoor UT. d2d_in gives the outdoor distance d2D - d2D-in for los_probability (call o2i_loss first) and is the input of the legacy outdoor distance of path_loss
  • Applicability (Table 7.4.3-2): RMa uses low only, InF high only; UMa, UMi: low and high; SMa: low, high and low_A. TR maximum indoor distance: 25 m for UMa, UMi and SMa commercial buildings, 10 m for RMa and SMa residential buildings (conf-file key O2I_d2D_in_max). The TR SMa layout has 90 % residential and 10 % commercial buildings (Table 7.2-5): split the UTs by building type and call o2i_loss once per type
  • Outputs must not share memory with the inputs or with each other
  • Validation, in this order: fc non-empty, finite and > 0; rnd with 4 columns, columns 0 to 2 in [0, 1], column 3 finite; models non-empty, each a known name; weights with one finite element >= 0 per model and a sum of 1 within 1e-6; d2d_in_max finite and >= 0. All checks run before any output is written

path_loss

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Path loss and shadow-fading standard deviation of a set of links

  • Evaluates one of the 10 parametric path-loss models of the QuaDRiGa conf files for every link and carrier frequency. pl_model and plpar are the values of PL_model and the PL_ keys (without the prefix) as returned by conf_file_read; the TR 38.901 v19.5.0 conf files in data/config reproduce Table 7.4.1-1 with them
  • Notation: f = fc / 1e9 in GHz (not limited by LSP_fc_min); d3, d2 the 3D and 2D distance in m; hBS, hUT the z coordinates of Tx and Rx (no ground model); [X] the value of key X, or its default if the key is missing (X = v in the lists below); PL1(x) = A1·lg(x) + B + C·lg(f) + D·x; sf the shadow-fading std
  • Models, required keys and defaults:
    • constant (A): pl = A
    • logdist (A, B, C; SF optional): pl = A·lg(d3) + B + C·lg(f); sf = [SF] if present
    • logdist_simple (A, B): pl = A·lg(d3) + B
    • winner_los (A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, C2, D1, D2, E1, E2, F1, F2, sig1, sig2): hb = max(hBS, 1.5), hm = max(hUT, 1.5) of each link; G = B1 + C1·lg f + D1·lg hb + E1·lg hm, H = B2 + C2·lg f + D2·lg hb + E2·lg hm, breakpoint bp = 10^((H - G)/(A1 - A2)); d2 <= bp: pl = A1·lg d2 + G + F1·hm, sf = sig1; else pl = A2·lg d2 + H + F2·hm, sf = sig2 (continuous at bp for F1 = F2); A1 and A2 must differ
    • winner_nlos (A1..A3, Ah1..Ah3, B1..B3, C1..C3, D1..D3, E1..E3, F1..F3): hb, hm as winner_los; L_j = (A_j + Ah_j·lg hb)·lg d2 + B_j + C_j·lg f + D_j·lg hb + E_j·lg hm + F_j·hm; pl = L_1 for f < 1.5, L_2 for 1.5 <= f < 2, L_3 for f >= 2
    • winner_pathloss (A, B, C, X; SF optional): pl = A·lg d3 + B + C·lg(f/5) + X; sf = [SF] if present
    • dual_slope (A1 or A, B, E; A2 = A1, C = 0, D = 0, hE = 0, hE_rand = 0, sig1, sig2 optional): hb = max(hBS, 1.1·hE, 0.1), hm = max(hUT, 1.1·hE, 0.1); dBP = E·f·(hb - hE)·(hm - hE); d2 <= dBP: pl = PL1(d3), sf = [sig1]; d2 > dBP: pl = PL1(dBP3) + A2·lg(d3/dBP3), sf = [sig2] (each only if present), with the 3D breakpoint distance dBP3 = sqrt(dBP² + (hb - hm)²). This is Table 7.4.1-1 for UMa, UMi, InH and InF; for RMa and SMa LOS the TR uses the 2D breakpoint distance in PL2, which differs by at most 0.034 dB over the TR ranges
    • tripple_slope (A1 or A, B, E1 or E; A2 = A1, A3 = A2, C = 0, D = 0, E2 = E1, hE1 = 0, hE2 = 0, sig1..sig3 optional): hb = max(hBS, 1.1·hE1, 1.1·hE2, 0.1), hm the same; dBPj = Ej·f·(hb - hEj)·(hm - hEj), dBP1 = min(dBP1, dBP2), dBPj3 = sqrt(dBPj² + (hb - hm)²); LBP1 = PL1(dBP13), LBP2 = LBP1 + A2·lg(dBP23/dBP13); d2 <= dBP1: PL1(d3), sf = [sig1]; dBP1 < d2 <= dBP2: LBP1 + A2·lg(d3/dBP13), sf = [sig2]; d2 > dBP2: LBP2 + A3·lg(d3/dBP23), sf = [sig3]
    • nlos (An, Bn; the dual_slope keys if LOSmax != 0; Cn, Dn, D1n, D2n, D3n, En, E1n, E2n, E3n, Fn, G1n = 0, G2n = 1, LOSmax = 1, sig optional; Ax, Bx, Cx = 0): hb = max(hBS, 0.1), hm = max(hUT, 0.1); PLn = An·lg d3 + Bn + Cn·lg f + Dn·lg hb + D1n·lg(hb)/hb + D2n·lg(hb)/hb² + D3n·hb + En·lg hm + E1n·lg(hm)/hm + E2n·lg(hm)/hm² + E3n·hm + Fn·lg(hb)·lg(d3) + G1n·(lg(G2n·hm))²; pl = PLn; if [LOSmax] != 0: pl = max(pl, PL_LOS) with the dual_slope loss of the same parameters (incl. the random hE); if Ax, Bx or Cx is present: pl = max(pl, Ax·lg d3 + Bx + Cx·lg f) (e.g. the InF-SL term of InF-DL); sf = [sig] if present
    • satellite (A = 20, B = 32.45, C = 20, D = 0, usePLa = 1): sa = min(hBS / d3, 1) with the absolute Tx height; pl = +Inf if sa <= 0; else pl = A·lg d3 + B + C·lg f + D·lg(asin(sa)) + PLa with PLa = Z(f) / sa if usePLa != 0, else 0; Z(f) is the zenith attenuation by atmospheric gases (93 values from 1 to 100 GHz, linear interpolation, constant beyond both ends)
    • empty pl_model: pl = 0
  • New keys of the TR 38.901 v19 files: hE_rand (non-zero: random environment height of UMa), LOSmax (0: no maximum with the LOS term in nlos), Ax, Bx, Cx (additional term in the maximum of nlos)
  • Random environment height (TR 38.901 Table 7.4.1-1, note 1), in dual_slope and the LOS term of nlos when [hE_rand] != 0 and rnd_he is given, per link with u = rnd_he(l), d = d2, raw hUT: g = 0 for d <= 18, else 1.25·(d/100)³·exp(-d/150); C' = 0 for hUT < 13, ((hUT - 13)/10)^1.5 for hUT <= 23, else 1; C = C'·g, p1 = 1/(1 + C); n = size of the set {12, 15, ..., hUT - 1.5}; hE = 1 if C = 0, n = 0, u < p1 or p1 rounds to 1 (C below 1.1e-16, e.g. beyond about 7.5 km at hUT = 20), else hE = 12 + 3·min(floor((u - p1)/(1 - p1)·n), n - 1). The UT height is then clamped to hm = max(hUT, hE + 0.1, 0.1) instead of 1.1·hE: for hE = 1 this is the fixed-hE clamp (also below hUT = 1.1), and the drawn heights 12, 15, ... are not affected (hUT - hE >= 1.5). Without rnd_he the fixed [hE] is used. rnd_he is column 10 of lsf_draw, a spatially consistent uniform value: TR 38.901 draws hE independently per link and gives no decorrelation distance; the library makes it spatially consistent in the sense of clause 7.6.3 with the decorrelation distance SF_lambda, so nearby UTs of a site share hE. Along a track hE switches between its discrete values where u crosses a threshold, and the loss beyond the breakpoint steps there; evaluate rnd_he once per track segment to avoid this
  • Distances: d3, d2 are the geometric distances (TR 38.901 eq. 7.4-1: for an indoor UT d3D-out + d3D-in). If d2d_in is given (legacy mode), a link with d2d_in(l) > 0 uses the outdoor distance instead: din = min(d2d_in, d2), d3in = d3·din/d2 (d3 if d2 = 0), limited to d3; if d3 - d3in < 10: d3in = d3 - 10 (minimum outdoor distance 10 m), then max(d3in, 0); p = d3in/d3 (0 if d3 = 0); d3 = d3 - d3in, d2 = d2·(1 - p). A link with d2d_in(l) = 0 is an outdoor link and keeps the geometric distances (no 10 m rule). Then d3 = max(d3, 0.1), d2 = max(d2, 0.1). The O2I penetration loss is not added; add the output of o2i_loss
  • Default shadow-fading std, where a model does not set it: the SF std of the LSP formula of lsp_generate with the geometric distance, sf = max(0, max(0, SF_sigma + SF_delta·lg(SF_omega + f')) + SF_kappa·lg(d) + SF_tau·lg(h) + SF_beta·lg(atan(h/d))) with d = max(d2D, 1e-4), h = max(hBS, 1e-4), f' = max(f, LSP_fc_min); for scenario files without such terms this is SF_sigma. Passing sf_sigma to lsp_generate is then neutral. With sf_sigma requested, SF_sigma, SF_delta, SF_kappa, SF_tau, SF_beta must be finite, and a frequency term with SF_delta != 0 requires a finite SF_omega and SF_omega + f' > 0
  • Validation: positions, fc, the lengths of d2d_in and rnd_he, their values, the model name, the parameters of the model in the order the model reads them (a required key that is missing throws Path-loss model '<model>' requires the parameter '<key>'., naming A1 for "A1 or A" and E1 for "E1 or E"; every key that the model reads must have exactly one value, which must be finite; keys not read are ignored), the breakpoint factors E, E1, E2 and G2n of nlos (> 0) and A1 != A2 of winner_los, then scenpar (scenpar_validate, its messages pass through), then the SF coefficients and frequency term if sf_sigma is requested. All checks run before any output is written
  • The models are evaluated as written for any positive frequency, also outside their validity range
  • Outputs must not share memory with the inputs or with each other

scenpar_validate

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Validate scenario parameters and complete them with default values

  • Checks a set of QuaDRiGa scenario parameters that did not come from a conf file and adds every missing key with its default value, so that scenpar has all n_key = 171 entries on return
  • An empty scenpar returns the complete default parameter set
  • A set with the 138 numeric keys of QuaDRiGa is completed with the 33 keys for 3GPP TR 38.901 v19.5.0, which have no effect at their default of 0
  • A name in scenpar that is not one of the 171 keys is an error, also with validate = false; this includes the QuaDRiGa key GR_epsilon, which is not supported
  • Value checks with validate = true; NaN is an error for every key:
    • Integer from 1 to 1000: NumClusters, NumSubPaths
    • Finite and > 0: r_DS
    • Finite and >= 0: the 8 decorrelation distances (DS_lambda ... XPR_lambda), SC_lambda, absTOA_lambda, PerClusterDS, PerClusterDS_min, PerClusterAS_D, PerClusterAS_A, PerClusterES_D, PerClusterES_A, LNS_ksi, LOS_scatter_radius, GR_enabled, LSP_fc_min, EoD_offset_b, EoD_offset_hcl, PerClusterDS_fc_min, PerClusterES_D_scale, absTOA_Lmax, NF_alpha, NF_beta, SNS_sigma, SNS_A, SNS_B, SNS_R, SNS_delta_var, PolVar_sigma, LOS_state_lambda, IO_state_lambda, O2I_d2D_in_max, DS_VS, DS_VS_a, DS_VS_b
    • Integer from 0 to 1000: NumClusters_min, NF_k1
    • In the range from 0 to 1: SNS_mu
    • In the range from -1 to 1: the 28 correlations (asD_ds to xpr_esa)
    • All other keys accept any value including Inf and -Inf
    • NumClusters_min must not exceed NumClusters
    • NF_alpha and NF_beta must be both 0 or both > 0
    • DS_VS_a and DS_VS_b must not both be 0 if DS_VS is > 0
    • subpath_method must be legacy, Laplacian or mmMAGIC
  • With validate = false no value is checked: NaN and any subpath_method are accepted
  • The symmetric matrix lsp_xcorr is built from the 28 correlation keys and has a unit diagonal. It is tested by a Cholesky factorization. A matrix that is not positive definite is not an error.
  • Throws std::invalid_argument; a failed call leaves scenpar and the outputs untouched

Declaration

bool quadriga_lib::scenpar_validate(
    std::unordered_map<std::string, double> &scenpar,
    const std::string &subpath_method = "legacy",
    arma::mat *lsp_xcorr = nullptr,
    std::vector<std::string> *key_order = nullptr,
    bool validate = true);

Inputs

scenpar
Numeric scenario parameters; updated in-place: given values are kept, missing keys are added with their default; n_key = 171 entries on return
subpath_methodoptional
Value of SubpathMethod, the only parameter that is not numeric
validateoptional
false: only complete with defaults, no value checks

Outputs

lsp_xcorroptional
LSP cross-correlation matrix; order of rows and columns: DS, KF, SF, ASD, ASA, ESD, ESA, XPR; [8, 8]
key_orderoptional
Canonical order of the keys in scenpar: the QuaDRiGa order without SubpathMethod (its position is between elements 105 and 106, 0-based), then the 33 new keys; [n_key]

Returns

  • true if lsp_xcorr is positive definite (all 8 pivots of the factorization are > 0); false also if it contains NaN

See also

  • conf_file_read (read the parameters from a conf file)
  • conf_file_write (applies the same checks before writing)

ssf_clusters

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Cluster delays, powers and angles of a set of links (TR 38.901 clause 7.5 steps 5 to 7)

  • Turns the LSPs of lsp_generate and the random values of ssf_draw into the clusters of each link, by one of three methods:
    • "38.901" (default): TR 38.901 clause 7.5 steps 5 to 7 at one frequency, for drop-based calibration. Clusters 25 dB below the strongest get power 0 (no renormalisation); the K-factor in the scaling factors is limited to

      = -5 dB. Under spatial consistency (clause 7.6.3.1) evaluate the blocks 1 to 8 of rnd at the drop or segment start and keep them along the track

    • "38.901_MF": TR 38.901 clause 7.6.5.1 as written, with the anchor LSPs lsp_anchor; where the multi-frequency method of the TR is required
    • "quadriga": S. Jaeckel et al., "A Spatially Consistent Geometric D2D Small-Scale Fading Model for Multiple Frequencies", 2019, with the LOS direction added to the cluster offsets; for tracks, several frequencies and device-to-device links
Property "38.901" "38.901_MF" "quadriga"
Continuous along tracks no NLOS only yes
Same delays and angles at all frequencies n/a NLOS, or K the same at all frequencies yes
Output spreads equal the input spreads no no DS, and AS below the caps, at one frequency without ground reflection
Per-cluster shadowing yes yes, per frequency no
  • Slots per link: 0 = LOS path, 1 = ground reflection if GR_enabled > 0 (G = 1), then the N = NumClusters - 1 NLOS clusters; n_slot = NumClusters + G. Slot 1 + G + n belongs to column n of each block of rnd (no sorting). Clusters n >= n_cluster(l) (TR clause 7.6.15) get delay 0, power 0 and the LOS angles. Identify the LOS path by its slot, never by delay or path length: NLOS clusters of the TR methods can have delay 0
  • A scenario is LOS if KF_mu > -30 dB. In an NLOS scenario the LOS and ground-reflection powers are 0 whatever lsp holds (NumClusters > 1); legacy QuaDRiGa "NLOS" files with KF_mu > -30 run as LOS
  • Delays in [s] relative to the LOS delay d3D/c; angles in [rad], GCS, elevation convention; slot 0 holds the geometric LOS direction. Powers are the coefficient powers of TR eq. (7.5-30), LOS K/(K+1), NLOS clusters P_n/(K+1), without path loss and shadow fading
  • Absolute TOA (TR clause 7.6.9), NLOS scenarios only: "38.901", "38.901_MF" add abs_toa(l) to the NLOS delays; "quadriga" places the first NLOS cluster at abs_toa(l) (where absTOA_mu <= -30: only where abs_toa(l) > 0)
  • Ground reflection (TR clause 7.6.8) on the plane z = 0. Slot power K/(K+1)·(d3D/d_GR)²·R² (TR methods, on top of the other slots) or K/(K+1)·R² ("quadriga") with R² = (abs(R_par)² + abs(R_perp)²)/2 of TR eqs. (7.6-38), (7.6-39). The coefficient is sqrt(power)·diag(R_par, -R_perp)/R, without polarisation sqrt(power)·exp(j·arg(R_par))
  • NumClusters = 1: the LOS path only, power 1 in all scenarios (K/(K+1) = 1, also in the ground-reflection power), plus the ground reflection if enabled; rnd, rnd_freq and lsp_anchor may be empty
  • Swap reciprocity: with mirrored random values (dual mobility in ssf_draw) and mirrored LSPs, swapping tx_pos and rx_pos exchanges the departure and arrival angles ("38.901": eod_offset_deg = 0 and no O2I link; "quadriga": eod_offset_deg = 0)
  • scenpar, lsp, rnd and rnd_freq must come from the same scenario (only sizes are checked); scenpar is validated by scenpar_validate. Outputs must not share memory with the inputs

Declaration

ssf_draw

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Spatially correlated normalized random values of one small-scale fading generator set at a set of links

  • Evaluates a set of ssf_init_phases at the links with the rules of lsf_draw for single and dual mobility, floors, 2D/3D mode and precision; every generator uses the decorrelation distance SC_lambda (TR 38.901 Table 7.6.3.1-2; 0 = spatial consistency off, used as 0.1 m)
  • Columns, N = NumClusters - 1; column b·N + n belongs to block b and NLOS cluster n:
    • shared set (set_id = -1, 9·N columns): block 0 cluster delay, Uniform(0,1); blocks 1, 2 sign of AOD, AOA; 3, 4 sign of ZOD, ZOA; 5, 6 angle offset of AOD, AOA; 7, 8 angle offset of ZOD, ZOA; Normal(0,1)
    • per-frequency set (set_id = k, N columns): cluster shadowing, Normal(0,1)
  • Dual mobility: swapping tx_pos and rx_pos exchanges the blocks 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6, 7 and 8 and keeps the delay and shadowing blocks, exactly (D2D reciprocity of S. Jaeckel et al., "A Spatially Consistent Geometric D2D Small-Scale Fading Model for Multiple Frequencies", 2019)
  • A column depends neither on the other columns nor on the other links; later versions append blocks and keep the values of the existing columns
  • preset, horizontal and the set type must match ssf_init_phases. NumClusters = 1 gives [n_link, 0] (any empty phase is accepted)

ssf_init_phases

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Draw the random phases of one small-scale fading generator set of a BS site and scenario

  • The cluster random values of the small-scale fading (TR 38.901 clause 7.6.3.1) come in two kinds of sets, with N = NumClusters - 1 NLOS clusters: one shared cluster set (set_id = -1, 9·N generators) and one set per carrier frequency (set_id = k, N generators, k = index in the caller's frequency list, the same order in every call). ssf_draw evaluates the phases at the links and lists the columns
  • The phases are a fixed function of seed, the seed of the large-scale set of the same site and scenario (lsf_init_phases), and set_id, equal on all platforms; the sets do not repeat the large-scale phases and are independent of each other. Keep an explicit seed (or the phase cubes) to reproduce the clusters
  • Each scenario of a site (LOS, NLOS, O2I) needs its own large-scale seed: TR 38.901 clause 7.6.3.4 makes the link types uncorrelated
  • NumClusters = 1: both sets are empty

fast_cart2geo

#
Also inC++MATLAB –Python –Markdown

Convert elementwise Cartesian coordinates to azimuth/elevation angles and vector length

  • Conversion: len = sqrt(x² + y² + z²), az = atan2(y, x), el = asin(clamp(z / len, -1, 1))
  • Inputs are arbitrary 3D vectors (not required to be unit-length); len returns the Euclidean norm
  • z/len is clamped to [-1, 1] before asin to guard against len == 0 and FMA rounding artefacts pushing abs(z/len) slightly above 1
  • All inputs must have the same length
  • AVX2 kernel computes the angles in single precision (double outputs are cast back from float); for dtype=double, len and z / len are computed in double precision, so very small or very large vectors keep their direction; GENERIC kernel preserves full dtype precision
  • Azimuth in [-pi, pi] (atan2 special values as in fast_atan2); NaN input gives NaN in az, el and len

fast_sincos

#
Also inC++MATLABPython –Markdown

Compute elementwise approximate sine and/or cosine of a vector

  • AVX2-optimized (8 floats/lane); scalar fallback without AVX2
  • Max absolute error about 1.3e-7 (2^-22.9) against the exact sine / cosine of the input value for |x| <= 1e10 (both kernels; the argument is reduced in double precision where single precision is not enough)
  • Results stay in [-1, 1] for all finite x; inf and NaN give NaN
  • The AVX2 kernel is fastest for |x| <= 2^22 (4.2e6); larger arguments take about 1.5 times as long
  • Either s or c may be nullptr to skip that computation

fast_slerp

#
Also inC++MATLAB –Python –Markdown

Compute elementwise approximate SLERP interpolation between two complex-valued vectors

  • Interpolates phase via SLERP on normalized directions; amplitudes are linearly interpolated
  • Weight w=0 returns A, w=1 returns B; per-element weights in [0, 1]
  • Near-antipodal inputs (phase difference close to pi) fall back to linear interpolation smoothly
  • If both input amplitudes are negligible (below 1.19e-7), output is zero
  • Max relative error vs. double-precision reference about 5e-7 for phase differences up to 2 rad, 1.2e-5 up to 3 rad; larger towards the near-antipodal transition to linear interpolation
  • The result of an element does not depend on the other elements
  • AVX2-optimized (8 complex pairs/lane); scalar fallback without AVX2

interp_2D

#
Also inC++MATLAB –Python –Markdown

Perform linear interpolation (1D or 2D) on single or multiple data sets

  • Interpolates given input data at specified output points.
  • Outside the range of the input sample points, the nearest end value is returned (constant extrapolation); output sample points that are NaN give NaN.
  • The input sample points need not be sorted (they are sorted internally); repeated values are allowed; they must be finite.
  • Supports single and multiple data sets.
  • Returns interpolated results either directly or through reference argument.
  • Data types (dtype): float or double

Declarations

void interp_2D(const arma::Cube<dtype> &input, const arma::Col<dtype> &xi, const arma::Col<dtype> &yi,
               const arma::Col<dtype> &xo, const arma::Col<dtype> &yo, arma::Cube<dtype> &output);

arma::Cube<dtype> interp_2D(const arma::Cube<dtype> &input, const arma::Col<dtype> &xi, const arma::Col<dtype> &yi,
                            const arma::Col<dtype> &xo, const arma::Col<dtype> &yo);

arma::Mat<dtype> interp_2D(const arma::Mat<dtype> &input, const arma::Col<dtype> &xi, const arma::Col<dtype> &yi,
                           const arma::Col<dtype> &xo, const arma::Col<dtype> &yo);

arma::Mat<dtype> interp_1D(const arma::Mat<dtype> &input, const arma::Col<dtype> &xi, const arma::Col<dtype> &xo);

arma::Col<dtype> interp_1D(const arma::Col<dtype> &input, const arma::Col<dtype> &xi, const arma::Col<dtype> &xo);

Arguments

  • input: Input data array/matrix (size details below)
  • xi: Input x-axis sampling points, vector of length nx
  • yi: Input y-axis sampling points (for 2D only), vector of length ny
  • xo: Output x-axis sampling points, vector of length mx
  • yo: Output y-axis sampling points (for 2D only), vector of length my
  • output: Interpolated data cube (modified in-place for one variant)

Input / Output size details

  • 2D interpolation of multiple datasets (arma::Cube): input: [ny, nx, ne]; output: [my, mx, ne]
  • 2D interpolation of single dataset (arma::Mat): input: [ny, nx]; output: [my, mx]
  • 1D interpolation of multiple datasets (arma::Mat): input: [nx, ne]; output: [mx, ne]
  • 1D interpolation of single dataset (arma::Col): input: [nx], output: [mx]

Examples

  • 2D interpolation example:
arma::cube input(5, 5, 2, arma::fill::randu); // example input data
arma::vec xi = arma::linspace(0, 4, 5);
arma::vec yi = arma::linspace(0, 4, 5);
arma::vec xo = arma::linspace(0, 4, 10);
arma::vec yo = arma::linspace(0, 4, 10);

arma::cube output;
quadriga_lib::interp_2D(input, xi, yi, xo, yo, output);
  • 1D interpolation example:
arma::vec input = arma::linspace(0, 1, 5);
arma::vec xi = arma::linspace(0, 4, 5);
arma::vec xo = arma::linspace(0, 4, 10);

auto output = quadriga_lib::interp_1D(input, xi, xo);

Site-specific simulation tools

calc_diffraction_gain

#
Also inC++MATLABPythonMarkdown

Calculate diffraction gain for multiple TX-RX pairs using a 3D triangular mesh

  • Estimates diffraction gain by evaluating Fresnel ellipsoid obstruction; each TX-RX path is divided into n_path elliptic-arc paths (controlled by lod), each approximated by n_seg line segments
  • Segment attenuation is combined via weighted summation calibrated to 2D UTD coefficients, generalized to arbitrary 3D shapes
  • Optional sub-mesh indexing (see triangle_mesh_segmentation) accelerates computation by skipping triangles whose bounding box does not intersect the TX-RX path

Declaration

void calc_diffraction_gain(
    const arma::Mat<dtype> &orig,
    const arma::Mat<dtype> &dest,
    const arma::Mat<dtype> &mesh,
    const arma::uvec &mtl_ind,
    const std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<dtype>> &mtl_prop,
    dtype center_frequency,
    int lod = 2,
    arma::Col<dtype> *gain = nullptr,
    arma::Mat<dtype> *xprmat = nullptr,
    arma::Cube<dtype> *coord = nullptr,
    int verbose = 0,
    const arma::u32_vec *sub_mesh_index = nullptr,
    int use_kernel = 0,
    int gpu_id = 0,
    bool scalar_mode = false,
    double thin_slab_threshold = 0.0,
    bool apply_fspl = false,
    bool apply_phase = false);

Inputs

orig
TX positions; [n_pos, 3]
dest
RX positions; [n_pos, 3]
mesh
Triangle vertices, each row {x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2,x3,y3,z3}; [n_mesh, 9]
mtl_ind
1-based material index per face, 0 = no material (the csv_ind output of obj_file_read); [n_mesh]
mtl_prop
Material properties keyed by column name (the csv_prop output of obj_file_read); each value has length n_mtl
center_frequency
Center frequency in [Hz]. In EM mode the electromagnetic frequency. In scalar (acoustic) mode the EM-equivalent frequency f_eq = f_acoustic · c_light / c_sound (c_light = 299 792 458 m/s, c_sound = 342.76271 m/s), so that c_light / f_eq is the acoustic wavelength; this is the frequency unit of ray_mesh_interact, ray_progress and generate_diffraction_paths in scalar mode. Passing the acoustic frequency itself gives a wavelength 874 636 times too long. The MATLAB and Python wrappers take the acoustic frequency and convert it.
lod
Level of detail (0–7), controls n_path and n_seg; 0 = direct ray only (n_path = 1, n_seg = 1); 1–7 as in the table of generate_diffraction_paths
verbose
Verbosity level
sub_mesh_index
0-based sub-mesh index for acceleration; see triangle_mesh_segmentation; [n_mesh]
use_kernel
Kernel selection: 0 = auto, 1 = GENERIC, 2 = AVX2, 3 = CUDA; error if unavailable
gpu_id
CUDA device ID; ignored for non-CUDA kernels
scalar_mode
If true, uses scalar transmission (TE-only reflection coefficient, energy-conservation transmission) instead of EM TE/TM averaging. Default false (EM mode). Selects interaction type passed to ray_mesh_interact (4 vs. 1).
thin_slab_threshold
Thin-slab (Fabry-Pérot) resolve threshold on the round-trip in-slab amplitude ρ: a series is summed where ρ ≥ eps; 0 = resolve always (default); eps ≥ 1 re-emits every series whose ρ is below one, and a round trip at or above one is always summed; see ray_state_update
apply_fspl
If true, folds the geometric spreading loss into gain, so that gain becomes an absolute propagation gain instead of a value relative to FSPL. Default false. The reference distance is the direct TX-RX distance, matching the path_length definition used by qrt_file_read for a transmission-only path. In EM mode the loss is 32.45 + 20·log10(f_GHz) + 20·log10(d_m) [dB]; in scalar mode it is 20·log10(d_m) + α(f)·d_m [dB], with α from ISO 9613-1 at T = 20 °C, RH = 50 %, p = 1 atm, evaluated at the acoustic frequency f = center_frequency · c_sound / c_light.
apply_phase
If true, multiplies xprmat by the propagation phase term exp(-j·2π·d/λ), using the same direct TX-RX distance d. Default false. The wavelength is λ = c_light / center_frequency in both modes; in scalar mode this is the acoustic wavelength because center_frequency is the EM-equivalent frequency (see above). Since the term has unit magnitude, xprmat stays normalized. This is the phase contribution that get_channels_spherical would otherwise add from path_length; enabling it here gives the complete omni-radiator coefficient without running the channel generator.

Outputs

gain
Diffraction gain per TX-RX pair, linear power scale; [n_pos]. Relative to FSPL by default, i.e. bounded by 0 and 1; absolute propagation gain when apply_fspl = true.
xprmat
Normalized polarization transfer matrix: the amplitude carries no path gain (max column power is 1), only the relative polarization coupling and phase. The gain output holds the power. For EM mode: interleaved complex, col-major [ReVV ImVV ReHV ImHV ReVH ImVH ReHH ImHH] with labels <rx><tx>: rows 0-1 = (V rx, V tx), rows 2-3 = (H rx, V tx), rows 4-5 = (V rx, H tx), rows 6-7 = (H rx, H tx), the row order of M in get_channels_spherical; [8, n_pos]; For scalar mode: scalar pressure coefficient [Re Im]; [2, n_pos]. With apply_phase = true, the propagation phase exp(-j·2π·d/λ) is applied on top; the normalization is unaffected because that term has unit magnitude.
coord
Diffracted path coordinates excluding endpoints; [3, n_seg-1, n_pos] with n_seg from lod (e.g. [3, 2, n_pos] for lod 2, [3, 9, n_pos] for lod 7, [3, 0, n_pos] for lod 0)

See also

  • generate_diffraction_paths (controls path/segment count via lod)
  • triangle_mesh_segmentation (generates sub_mesh_index)
  • obj_file_read (defines mtl_prop format)
  • ray_mesh_interact (used for media interactions)
  • qrt_file_read (same path-loss model, used by apply_fspl)
  • get_channels_spherical (applies the same propagation phase as apply_phase)

combine_irs_coord

#
Also inC++MATLAB –Python –Markdown

Combine path interaction coordinates for IRS-assisted TX → RX channels

  • Merges two propagation segments (TX → IRS and IRS → RX) into complete path interaction coordinate sequences
  • Interaction coordinates use a compressed format: no_interact counts interactions per path, interact_coord stores all coordinates sequentially in path order
  • Each combined path appends segment 1 coordinates (optionally reversed) then the IRS position then segment 2 coordinates (optionally reversed); reversing affects coordinate order only, not endpoint positions
  • Output contains at most n_path_1 × n_path_2 paths; active_path (typically the return value of get_channels_irs) reduces this to active combinations only
  • Typically used after get_channels_irs to produce interaction data for path visualization (e.g. in Blender) via coord2path

    arma::u32_vec *no_interact,
    arma::Mat<dtype> *interact_coord,

    bool reverse_segment_2 = false,
